phases.description: Follow ordered task contracts, operation modes, task-map prerequisites and user approval gates. Phase 3 starts empty; empty does not mean completed. tasks.name: 1.1 Confirm scope, connections and existing content
tasks.description:
Owner: Orchestrator. Mode: intake. Depends on: user start instruction. Reuse provided inputs; ask only for missing facts needed next. Record source URLs/pages, desktop/mobile/both selection, evidence root, repositoryMode and exact sandbox path. Default bundled target /workspace/repos/optimizely-nextjs-saas-template; explicit existing path takes precedence and must not be replaced. Collect secure connector/secret references, CMS SaaS tenant/environment/application/root/locales and available read/write/preview capabilities; never paste credentials in chat or evidence. Ask whether existing models/content should be reused, updated or created separately; deletion is never implied. Capture mixed editorial freedom, shared header/footer update/variant policy, blueprint need and preview fallback preference. Significant external changes need per-batch user approval after a concrete diff, not blanket intake consent. Resolve four actual agent IDs and seeded tasks, assign agents and preserve rank. Store task-level prerequisites and stable task keys in a task map: recipe task schema lacks native owners/dependencies. Native phase dependencies remain. Missing CMS access blocks tenant work, not independent capture. Completion: readable brief, scoped missing inputs and actual task routing. Follow the operation-contract; preserve this task description and append actual results separately. Record evidence under the confirmed sandbox evidence root. A task status or agent receipt is not acceptance.

Record actual source URL(s), device/behavior scope, repository mode and requested target in the project brief; downstream tasks consume these values, not example-site defaults.

Release 1.5.5 requirements:
Confirm visual fidelity/device/state scope, source asset/font reuse and missing-resource substitution policy. Record existing media/model policy and connections; do not require secrets in documents.

tasks.name: 1.2 Prepare the bundled code template
tasks.description:
Owner: Developer. Depends on: 1.1 Confirm scope, connections and existing content. Read optimizely-nextjs/references/bundled-template.md and its pnpm-bootstrap.md procedure for setup and use its shipped prepare-template.mjs helper and template-bundle.json. In bundled mode materialize the template at the exact target from the brief (default /workspace/repos/optimizely-nextjs-saas-template). The helper validates integrity and refuses unrelated existing directories; reruns preserve edits. In existing mode skip extraction and reuse the supplied repository with its own package manager, lockfile, supported checks and actual source paths; bundled pnpm commands apply only to bundled mode. Never clone GitHub, run create-app, overwrite existing code or substitute another starter. Run the locked dependency install from the target, then local type and lint checks as documented; record exact commands, results, actual runtime/package versions and lock hash in a small setup receipt under evidence. Save the exact prepared path in the project brief. Separate recipeVersion=1.5.0 from SDK/CLI versions. Do not read node_modules routinely; dependency records and supplied source patterns suffice. Do not dump the bundle JSON into the conversation. Missing registry access blocks installation only: retain successful extraction, report the error and allow capture/annotation to proceed. No CMS login, opti-push, tenant seed, publication or deployment. A source template requiring CMS data is not a working mock preview; record that limitation. Completion requires prepared/reused code and successful applicable checks. If checks are blocked, keep setup pending/blocked and let independent capture continue; never mark blocked checks passed. On retry resume the failed step rather than re-extract/reinstall unchanged successful steps. In bundled mode, recover missing pnpm with scripts/ensure-pnpm.sh: reuse exact 12.5.1 or bootstrap it with npm in a separate writable tools prefix. Record its absolute executable and reuse it in new shells. npm tool bootstrap is allowed; application npm install or lockfile conversion is not. One bounded attempt before reporting a concrete blocker; no sudo, global installation or Corepack assumption. Preserve extraction and resume dependency install/checks from the failed stage. Mode: setup. Preparation is not permission to implement components. Keep the historical template provenance separate from the active recipe version.

tasks.name: 1.3 Capture source pages and section references
tasks.description:
Owner: QA. Mode: discovery. Depends on: 1.1 confirmed source/device scope. Use Playwright. Inspect and handle cookie consent before capture (accept/reject/remove as appropriate); record the action and verify no blocking banner/overlay. Capture each approved page at the confirmed desktop/mobile/both scope, full page plus useful section crops, with actual viewport/DPR/time/URL/state. Use consistent fonts/loaded assets and account for lazy loading/sticky elements. Do not invent a selector or no-action consent outcome. Inspect completeness/readability; preserve section references and source coordinates. Reuse valid captures, recapture only defects or approved state/device needs. Setup dependency-install failure does not prevent independent capture. Completion: unobstructed raw evidence and capture receipt, not screenshots alone. Follow the operation-contract; preserve this task description and append actual results separately. Record evidence under the confirmed sandbox evidence root. A task status or agent receipt is not acceptance.

Capture matching screenshots plus selected styles, exact visible text, image/background/font inventory and availability in one bounded session. Qualify ancestor/pseudo layers and clipping where needed. Record browser, fonts, image decode and state. Missing evidence remains explicit; reuse original full-page and section captures.

tasks.name: 1.4 Annotate components and create the inventory
tasks.description:
Owner: QA. Mode: discovery. Depends on: 1.3 Capture source pages and section references. Apply website-visual-qa/references/component-annotation.md and assets/annotation-inventory.template.md. Reuse accepted source screenshots/crops; no prior annotation filename is required. Discover the supplied page's actual sections, reusable component families, variants and occurrences. Produce a readable full-page component overview and section images labeling meaningful internal elements (text, media/icons, actions and controls when observed). Every meaningful visible element, including every action, must be in the inventory with a stable element ID, owning occurrence, observed role/text, evidence reference, candidate field/presentation role and observation status. If a visual label would obscure content, retain exact evidence and a label omission reason. Never invent absent fields or duplicate section actions into repeated items. A full-card link is not automatically an extra CTA for each decorative arrow. Preserve verbatim observed text separately from semantic names; unknown destinations/behavior remain unknown. Repeated definitions share a component ID, with distinct occurrence IDs, parent relationships and variant differences; an element box does not imply a CMS type. Inspect one representative per family plus variants, compare remaining occurrences, and keep all occurrence field coverage traceable. Validate completeness, ownership, IDs, source-relative geometry and visual readability; bounds/hashes alone do not establish accuracy. Save revision-matched images and inventory under evidence, regenerate only affected derivatives, and preserve accepted captures. Present evidence and explicit coverage gaps for review; do not start modeling or implementation. Apply generic feedback across component families, not only the example named. No fixed URL, component list, field count or CTA count is prescribed. Mode: discovery. Use confirmed device scope. Capture observed formatting/link/list needs and a human-readable inventory, not automatic richText choices. Full overview and section annotations feed readable component docs; preserve all element coverage.

Release 1.5.5 requirements:
Record meaningful anatomy and element order, CTA/image placement and visible versus clipped/hidden content. DOM presence does not imply painted visibility. Preserve component/occurrence/element IDs and candidate fields without promoting all elements to components.

tasks.name: 1.5 Incorporate feedback and record approval
tasks.description:
Owner: QA. Depends on: 1.4 Annotate components and create the inventory. Use actual user feedback to revise annotations and inventory, preserving component/occurrence IDs. If already approved, carry that approval forward without unnecessary changes. Save the approved revision and exact decision reference/scope under evidence. Never infer approval from silence or a filename. Remain awaiting review until the user approves; unresolved feedback blocks only affected scope. Output approved annotation/inventory paths and revision hashes. Keep full-page overview, section images and inventory on the same approved revision. Preserve task instructions; append approval references as results. Confirm component/element coverage and ownership using the annotation contract; carry general feedback across families and keep exact observed text separate from proposed semantics. Mode: discovery. User annotation approval covers evidence, not source implementation.

tasks.name: 2.1 Document styles, assets and behavior
tasks.description:
Owner: QA. Mode: documentation. Depends on: 1.5 approved annotations. Document each component/variant at confirmed device scope using approved screenshots and selective live style extraction. Reuse existing session/evidence; sample representative families and variant differences. Record measured typography/colors/spacing/borders/assets, layout and interactions including focus/empty states; distinguish observed, inferred and unknown. Put reviewable visual sections in component handoffs and shared token references. Link bulky raw CSS/DOM instead of embedding it. Completion: every approved component has styling/asset/behavior coverage or a scoped explicit gap. No application edits. Follow the operation-contract; preserve this task description and append actual results separately. Record evidence under the confirmed sandbox evidence root. A task status or agent receipt is not acceptance.

Release 1.5.5 requirements:
## Visual fidelity contract
Use one current source baseline per route/device/state with capture hash, browser/viewport/DPR, consent, fonts, image readiness and scroll/interaction state. Preserve superseded revisions; never infer that a new live visit matches an old capture. Missing selectors mean incomplete evidence, not absent content. Reconcile pixels, element and ancestor styles, pseudo-elements, backgrounds, intrinsic assets and clipping before prescribing a disputed layout. DOM presence or bounding boxes do not prove painted visibility. Keep observed appearance, implementation inference and approved target separate.
Each component's primary Markdown handoff contains a concise visual contract: anatomy and reading order, container/full-bleed behavior, grid, typography and wrapping, spacing, imagery/crop, CTA placement, clipping/states, evidence links, agreed tolerances and known gaps. Exact values come from this project's source, never a previous website. Put source-equivalent approved text and assets in fixtures early; keep fixture provenance in data attributes or a separate review panel outside the comparison area. Approve missing-font/asset substitutions and their impact explicitly; missing evidence may block visual acceptance without blocking independent code.
Resolve fonts and content first, then structure/geometry, then fine styling. Implement component anatomy and CSS together. Prefer fixing the responsible rule over piling on overrides; shared CSS changes require consumer retests. Keep semantic DOM order and keyboard order coherent. Verify each component in intended page context and then the assembled page. Use source/target crops plus full-page context, overlays/diffs and measured deltas; align section-relative measurements for local defects and page-level measurements for assembly. Do not rescale images to hide differences or turn all measured heights into fixed CSS heights. Preserve content resilience and requested responsive scope.
QA compares the actual render to authoritative source evidence independently, not just the correction spec. Record technical, visual and CMS/editor status separately (pass, fail, blocked or accepted exception with scope). HTTP 200, build success, populated image src and correct DOM order are not visual acceptance. Inspect actual image decoding and fonts. A changed spec needs traced evidence and invalidation of affected checks; an old QA pass does not override contrary evidence. After two unsuccessful attempts on the same defect, stop speculative patching and perform focused evidence diagnosis before another edit.
Batch related edits; inspect affected rendered sections before repeating full builds. Run code checks appropriate to changes and final integration validation. Reuse unchanged captures/tool paths/SDK qualification. Do not regenerate documentation or broadly read SDK internals for visual defects. Manual task starts and external approval boundaries remain in force.

tasks.name: 2.2 Define readable component models and handoffs
tasks.description:
Owner: Developer. Mode: documentation. Depends on: 2.1 visual sections and 1.2 available setup evidence. Produce one Markdown handoff per reusable component, grouping occurrences/variants, plus a page architecture document and review index. Lead with purpose, screenshot, recognizable names, reusable-definition versus shared-instance policy and human-readable fields: purpose/example, type/rationale, required/localized, defaults/validation/editor controls. Choose types from editing needs across all fields, not field names; rich text only for justified formatting. Include complete supporting models, ownership, allowed placements/children, UI mappings and every annotation element disposition. Add a clearly separate technical section: exact repo paths, supplied qualified SDK pattern, first future implementation action and checks. Reuse setup qualification; record unverified mappings without editing source or executing generator/typecheck/build to qualify them. No src/config/registry changes, install, CMS writes or opti-push. Recipe/SDK/CLI/profile versions are distinct. Carry isList/component required/localized safeguards and partial coverage. Initial component packet about 1000-1500 tokens with conditional exact-heading detail; never omit requirements to meet token limits. Write sections incrementally and checkpoint. Completion: readable complete docs and explicit decisions; no application implementation. Follow the operation-contract; preserve this task description and append actual results separately. Record evidence under the confirmed sandbox evidence root. A task status or agent receipt is not acceptance.

Phase-start guard: execute only within the user-authorized phase/task scope recorded in the task map. Approval of an artifact is not permission to start another phase; delegated and resumed runs inherit this boundary.

Preserve one Markdown model/handoff per reusable component with complete property, editorial, styling and UI contracts. Also produce a focused shared-foundation handoff using website-visual-qa/assets/foundation-handoff.template.md, plus the page-assembly handoff. Each has an actual repository, qualified pattern, first action/check, exact conditional reference sections, approval provenance and classified gaps. Documentation only; no source edits.

Release 1.5.5 requirements:
## Media and CMS readiness contract
Inspect the actual tenant when read access is authorized. Reuse a suitable concrete media type, including built-in ImageMedia where present; create a custom _image/_video/_media-derived type only when absent or justified by approved metadata/extension needs. Base types and abstract contracts are not concrete upload contentType keys. If tenant access is unavailable, record the dependency as unverified; never assume absence or fabricate keys. Define media dependencies before uploads, synchronize the approved schema first and confirm via readback.
Each model handoff records field reference types/allowed types, concrete media dependency, upload container policy, source asset identity, alt/decorative ownership, crop/focal behavior, reuse and locale strategy. Do not invent locale branches unsupported by media. Usage-specific alternative text can belong on the consuming component; choose deliberately. Component reference fields do not upload binary files. Asset batches separately upload/reuse actual files, map returned identities to fields and verify MIME/decode/access in the intended preview and public contexts. Keep rights and substitutions explicit. Diagnose wrong binary URL, reference expansion, authentication, permissions and publication separately; never assume publishing is the only repair for draft media.
Each reusable component also declares intended placement (selectable section, nested component, reference/shared content or layout region), required composition behavior, renderer registration, display-template association/default/settings, media dependencies and preview mapping. Do not make every child section-selectable. Reuse documented qualified patterns; carry decisions into Phase 3 task acceptance instead of deferring them to composition.
Display templates may target base type, content type or node type. Inspect actual association and existing defaults/consumers, propose the scoped diff and verify readback. Never apply blanket isDefault:true or universal 'one per base type' rules; preserve unrelated defaults. No sample template may silently override approved source styling. Validate against the actual API/SDK contract without routine broad SDK reading.

## Shared rendering and integration qualification
Phase 3 implements CMS-ready models, placement configuration, media dependencies, registered renderers, delivery adapters and preview plumbing as well as visual UI. Local qualification is not proof of tenant/editor acceptance. Use typed, qualified Graph/SDK response shapes or sanitized real responses for contract fixtures; label assumptions. Exercise nested URLs/link labels, media references/binary URL resolution, missing values, display settings and shared content through production adapters. Do not claim exact tenant shape can only be considered after deployment.
Fixture and CMS paths use the same components/styles and normalized rendering model; transport adapters may differ. Place fixtures on an explicit test-only route so a static page cannot shadow the CMS canonical route. Keep production routes derived from the project brief. Propagate authorized draft/version/locale context to shared header/footer and related fetches; prevent shared draft caching. Invalid/expired preview authorization produces a clear diagnostic, never a silent published-only fallback that hides shared drafts. Do not expose tokens in logs/evidence.
After approved schema/assets, Task 4.4 qualifies one representative draft with section selection, media, link and shared chrome using existing appropriate content or a separately approved minimal bootstrap batch. Read back actual responses, reconcile adapters and verify the native CMS iframe edit/refresh path before broad composition in 4.5. This is not implicit permission for extra tenant writes or publication. Register the actual preview host via an approved batch and verify readback; ephemeral hosts require requalification if changed. Empty content and HTTP 200 are not proof. Preserve downloadable local fallback on unavailable Kajoo preview.
Task 4.5 composes remaining approved content only after qualification. Task 5.1 independently compares the actual CMS-driven page to source and verifies picker selection, edits, refresh, references/images and shared regions. Test published delivery separately after its approval. Late code fixes remain possible but must identify the violated contract, update affected evidence and be manually started as implementation tasks; do not disguise planned missing integration as normal styling work.

Documentation only in Phase 2. Populate complete per-component Markdown visual/CMS contracts and foundation/assembly handoffs; no source or tenant writes.

tasks.name: 2.3 Review editorial architecture and CMS composition
tasks.description:
Owner: Optimizely Specialist. Mode: documentation. Depends on: 2.2 component/page handoffs. Review field choice, requiredness/localization, supporting types, delivery mappings and readable tables. Define Experience/Page structure, section versus element versus supporting/shared component roles, actual composition eligibility and intended picker, shared default header/footer and optional variant references, mixed editorial freedom, constrained display styles and blueprint justification. Blueprint copies are detached, not live shared inheritance. Inspect relevant existing tenant models/content read-only when access exists; flag update/migration risks and affected consumers. No automatic base-type/property conversion. Record real tool capabilities and secure connection gaps. Reconcile proposed CMS behavior with observed website behavior and ensure production/preview/fixture rendering paths align. Send targeted document corrections to Developer via Orchestrator. Completion: architecture review and all unresolved coding/visual/tenant decisions labeled; no source or tenant writes. Follow the operation-contract; preserve this task description and append actual results separately. Record evidence under the confirmed sandbox evidence root. A task status or agent receipt is not acceptance.

Ask the user for approval of the concrete consolidated revision; technical agent review is not that approval. Check all approved elements have dispositions, property rules, CSS and composition ownership. Record actual actor/decision/revision/scope and gaps. Do not infer from silence or completion. Completion: user-approved handoff or explicitly scoped approval with dependent exclusions. Follow the operation-contract; preserve this task description and append actual results separately. Record evidence under the confirmed sandbox evidence root. A task status or agent receipt is not acceptance.

tasks.name: 2.5 Create component and page implementation tasks
tasks.description:
Owner: Orchestrator. Mode: documentation. Depends on: 2.4 actual user-approved handoff. Populate the existing empty Phase 3 idempotently using actual phase/role IDs. One Developer task per reusable component definition, grouping occurrences/variants; include sole mandatory component document path/revision, component IDs, model/property/placement rules, source screenshot/style references, exact prepared repository, verified SDK pattern, first source action/check, dependencies and acceptance. Add shared layout/preview work with site defaults/variants and shared production CSS. Add Assemble page and verify build depending on every required component/shared-layout task; QA source comparison after assembly and an assembled-result user review after fixes. Shared type/registry dependencies must be explicit and serialized where needed. Record stable component+scope task keys; reuse matching tasks on rerun and preserve user edits. Task creation does not start implementation; wait for user start instruction. Phase 4 requires completed generated work and assembly QA, not an empty Phase 3 status. Do not hardcode any source website components. Follow the operation-contract; preserve this task description and append actual results separately. Record evidence under the confirmed sandbox evidence root. A task status or agent receipt is not acceptance.

## Manual implementation starts
Task 2.5 produces recommendations only. Create/reuse implementation tasks and return a readable prerequisite and parallelism table, then stop. Do not launch agents or implementation tasks from Task 2.5.
The user manually starts each implementation task or explicitly selects a named set of task IDs to run together. A general Phase 3 start, approved plan, eligible task, completed prerequisite, callback or resumed checkpoint does not authorize automatic scheduling. If the selected tasks are unclear, return the eligible task list and wait for selection. Once a task is explicitly started, perform its routine local work without repeated permission requests and return at its review boundary. Do not start siblings, dependents, assembly or another group on completion. Keep already manually started independent tasks within their own scope.
Before executing a selected task, verify its prerequisites and shared-file ownership. If prerequisites are incomplete or another active task owns a conflicting shared file, report the exact blocker; do not claim the task is safe merely because it appears in a recommended group. Delegation within a selected task must preserve that task's scope. Approval gates for tenant changes, upload, publishing and deployment remain unchanged.
The plan must list actual task IDs/names, owner, prerequisite task IDs and acceptance evidence, owned files, shared-file conflicts, suggested parallel group, current readiness (ready/blocked/unknown), and what the user can start next. Use actual approved component contracts and project paths. Future groups are conditional recommendations, not a launch queue. Put unresolved shared-file changes in an explicit prerequisite or integration task. Assemble only after all required components and foundation work pass, and only when the user starts assembly. Report refreshed readiness after results without dispatching more work.

Each generated task must include exactly one primary handoff path/revision appropriate to its component, foundation or assembly scope, the actual repository and package-manager executable from setup, first source action/check, acceptance criteria, dependencies, owned files and conditional supporting references. Preserve one Markdown handoff per reusable component and distinguish coding blockers from visual or tenant gaps. Keep all site URLs, component names and paths derived from project records. Set implementation tasks to awaiting manual start, not running; planning completion is not implementation completion.

Release 1.5.5 requirements:
Add acceptance to every generated component task for its visual contract, media dependency, placement configuration, registration, adapter and local CMS-shaped fixtures. Foundation includes shared fonts, production styles, non-shadowing fixture route and shared preview context. Assembly requires whole-page source comparison and production-path rendering. Preserve one primary Markdown handoff per task and manual starts. Report technical/visual/local-CMS readiness separately; actual tenant verification remains Phase 4/5.

Do not disable security globally. Significant application settings or frontend deployment require user approval of their own batch. Keep preview tokens secret. If Kajoo preview fails, pause dependent CMS verification and have Developer deliver a downloadable runnable code archive with safe env example, locked tooling, assets, startup/local CMS connection guide and validation receipt. No secrets/logs/node_modules in archive. Await actual local preview evidence to resume; download or HTTP success alone does not pass preview acceptance. Follow the operation-contract; preserve this task description and append actual results separately. Record evidence under the confirmed sandbox evidence root. A task status or agent receipt is not acceptance. If no suitable draft exists, prepare a minimal preview-bootstrap draft batch and obtain user approval before creating it; record its ID and retain it for later composition or approved cleanup. This scoped bootstrap breaks the preview/content prerequisite cycle; it is not permission for broad content creation.

Release 1.5.5 requirements:
## Visual fidelity contract
Use one current source baseline per route/device/state with capture hash, browser/viewport/DPR, consent, fonts, image readiness and scroll/interaction state. Preserve superseded revisions; never infer that a new live visit matches an old capture. Missing selectors mean incomplete evidence, not absent content. Reconcile pixels, element and ancestor styles, pseudo-elements, backgrounds, intrinsic assets and clipping before prescribing a disputed layout. DOM presence or bounding boxes do not prove painted visibility. Keep observed appearance, implementation inference and approved target separate.
Each component's primary Markdown handoff contains a concise visual contract: anatomy and reading order, container/full-bleed behavior, grid, typography and wrapping, spacing, imagery/crop, CTA placement, clipping/states, evidence links, agreed tolerances and known gaps. Exact values come from this project's source, never a previous website. Put source-equivalent approved text and assets in fixtures early; keep fixture provenance in data attributes or a separate review panel outside the comparison area. Approve missing-font/asset substitutions and their impact explicitly; missing evidence may block visual acceptance without blocking independent code.
Resolve fonts and content first, then structure/geometry, then fine styling. Implement component anatomy and CSS together. Prefer fixing the responsible rule over piling on overrides; shared CSS changes require consumer retests. Keep semantic DOM order and keyboard order coherent. Verify each component in intended page context and then the assembled page. Use source/target crops plus full-page context, overlays/diffs and measured deltas; align section-relative measurements for local defects and page-level measurements for assembly. Do not rescale images to hide differences or turn all measured heights into fixed CSS heights. Preserve content resilience and requested responsive scope.
QA compares the actual render to authoritative source evidence independently, not just the correction spec. Record technical, visual and CMS/editor status separately (pass, fail, blocked or accepted exception with scope). HTTP 200, build success, populated image src and correct DOM order are not visual acceptance. Inspect actual image decoding and fonts. A changed spec needs traced evidence and invalidation of affected checks; an old QA pass does not override contrary evidence. After two unsuccessful attempts on the same defect, stop speculative patching and perform focused evidence diagnosis before another edit.
Batch related edits; inspect affected rendered sections before repeating full builds. Run code checks appropriate to changes and final integration validation. Reuse unchanged captures/tool paths/SDK qualification. Do not regenerate documentation or broadly read SDK internals for visual defects. Manual task starts and external approval boundaries remain in force.

Require native CMS picker, image selection/loading, draft edit/refresh and shared region checks under approved test scope. Compare the CMS-rendered page against the same source baseline; list deviations instead of a blanket pass.
